s: Seaside Grand Resort has received complaints about long waits at its restaurants, slow room service and understaffed housekeeping. Labor costs are rising, and the resort is considering a self-service check-in kiosk and mobile ordering.
The general manager (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to improve efficiency while keeping the resort's reputation for service.
p: Describe the use of technology in operations
Streamline work processes
Coordinate activities with those of other departments
Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs
Explain employee's role in expense control
n: Uses technology to reduce wait times without losing personal service
Maps guest touch points and removes delays
Coordinates housekeeping, front desk and restaurants
Compares costs and savings of new technology
Trains staff and involves them in cost control
q: Which guests might dislike the kiosks, and how would you serve them?
How would you decide what to automate first?

c: Lantern Hill Inn, a historic 45-room inn
s: Lantern Hill Inn depends on leisure travelers in summer and fall. Winter occupancy is 28%, and a nearby vacation rental company has attracted many families who used to book rooms at the inn. Several local restaurants have also cut their winter hours.
The owner (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend a marketing strategy to increase winter bookings.
p: Explain the concept of market and market identification
Describe factors used by marketers to position products/services
Explain the nature of a promotional plan
Explain factors affecting pricing decisions
Identify the elements of the promotional mix
n: Identifies winter markets: couples, remote workers, local events
Positions the inn's unique features such as fireplaces and history
Builds a plan with budget, channels and timeline
Uses seasonal pricing and packages
Uses email, social, partnerships and local promotion
q: Would you lower prices in winter? Why or why not?
How would you measure whether winter promotions worked?

c: Coastline Hotels, a group of six hotels
s: Coastline Hotels loses many front desk and housekeeping employees within six months. Many cite unpredictable schedules and limited chances to advance. Guest satisfaction scores are lower in properties with high turnover.
The vice president (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to reduce turnover.
p: Discuss the nature of human resources management
Orient new employees
Motivate team members
Explain possible advancement patterns for jobs
Explain the role of ethics in human resources management
n: Calculates the cost of turnover
Improves scheduling with earlier notice and shift swap tools
Creates cross-training and a visible career ladder
Offers recognition and feedback
Treats employees fairly and consistently
q: Would raising wages be enough? Why or why not?
How would you measure whether turnover is improving?

s: Grand Meridian Hotel received a viral review after a guest was told his reserved suite was unavailable. The hotel moved him to a smaller room and a front desk agent said 'that's our policy'. The review has 30,000 shares.
The general manager (judge) wants you and your partner to recommend how to respond to the guest and the public and how to prevent future overbooking problems.
f: The guest booked six months ago for an anniversary
The hotel overbooks by 5% to cover no-shows
Online reviews dropped from 4.6 to 4.2 stars
Two other guests complained of similar issues
p: Handle customer/client complaints
Interpret business policies to customers/clients
Demonstrate a customer service mindset
Determine ways of reinforcing the company's image through employee performance
Explain the role of ethics in customer relationship management
n: Responds publicly with a sincere apology and private outreach
Offers meaningful compensation
Reviews overbooking policy and sets guidelines for exceptions
Empowers agents to solve problems
Treats guests honestly and fairly
q: Should the hotel stop overbooking? Why or why not?
How should the front desk agent have handled the conversation?

s: Sunburst Water Park & Hotel is planning a new water slide. Last summer, a guest was injured in a minor collision at the existing slide, and the park's insurance premium rose 18%.
The general manager (judge) wants you and your partner to analyze the risks and recommend how to manage safety and liability.
p: Explain the nature of risk management
Conduct a risk assessment of an event
Maintain a safe work environment
Explain procedures for handling accidents
Describe legal issues affecting businesses
n: Identifies hazards, likelihood and consequences
Recommends training, inspection and clear rules
Plans emergency response and documentation
Considers waivers, signage and insurance
Balances guest enjoyment with safety
q: Would you open the slide before all safety checks are complete if the season is ending? Why?
How would you communicate safety rules without ruining the fun?
